title: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources)

sections.label: Year of Climate Action
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the weather reminds people of climate change and welcomes designating 2018 as the Year of Climate Action.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If nothing else can wake those who do not believe in these phenomena, I hope even if we escaped the floods, at least the chilly weather and howling winds will remind us of the climate change issues and the need to take responsibility in our environment.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am pleased that we are designating 2018 as the Year of Climate Action.

sections.label: Carbon Tax and energy efficiency
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister what the goals for energy efficiency are, noting the Carbon Tax aims to increase energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Carbon Tax is meant to increase our energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what are our goals for energy efficiency?

sections.label: Carbon Tax and utility bills
sections.summary: The speaker asks for an estimate of how much household utilities bills will be affected by the Carbon Tax.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can we have an estimate of how much household utilities bills will be affected by the Carbon Tax?

sections.label: Sustainable Singapore Blueprint water target
sections.summary: Under the Sustainable Singapore Blueprint, a target was set to lower household water demand to 140 litres per capita per day by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the Sustainable Singapore Blueprint, we have set a target to lower water demand for households to 140 litres per capita per day by 2030.

sections.label: Leaving a sick Earth
sections.summary: The speaker says a sick and coughing Earth will be left to the next generation and urges changing ways to reverse the trend.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, it looks like we will leave a sick and coughing Earth to the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must urgently change our ways and reverse this trend as much as we can.

sections.label: Climate action goals for 2018
sections.summary: The speaker notes 2018 is the Year of Climate Action and asks the Minister to share the Ministry's climate action goals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I took the opportunity to share that all of them, including me, can play a part in mitigating the impact of climate change.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that 2018 has been declared as the Year of Climate Action for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share with the House on the climate action goals that the Ministry is pursuing for 2018 and beyond?

sections.label: Coastal Adaptation Study delay
sections.summary: BCA began the Coastal Adaptation Study in 2013, due to finish end-2017, but completion was pushed to the second half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) commenced the Coastal Adaptation Study in 2013 and this was slated for completion in end-2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But this has since been pushed to the second half of 2018.

sections.label: Northeast monsoon rainfall projections
sections.summary: The second National Climate Change study models show northeast monsoon monthly rainfall may rise by 2100 under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5 scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the second National Climate Change study, models reveal that by the year 2100, monthly rainfall total during the northeast monsoon may increase, at worse, by 42.9% under the representative concentration pathway (RCP) 4.5 scenario, and by 67.5% under the RCP 8.5 scenario.

sections.label: Carbon tax and Paris commitment
sections.summary: Singapore committed under the Paris Agreement to cut emissions intensity by 36% by 2030 and announced a $5 per tonne carbon tax on large emitters.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under the Paris Climate Agreement, Singapore is committed to reducing our emissions intensity by 36% in 2030 compared to 2005 levels and also to stabilise our emission level.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In line with this commitment, it is announced in Budget 2018 that, next year, we will introduce a carbon tax of $5 per tonne of greenhouse gas emissions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The tax will also be applied upstream on large direct emitters, defined as those that emit 25,000 or more tonnes of greenhouse gases each year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: By that count, it was reported that between 30 to 40 emitters in Singapore will be affected.

sections.label: Carbon tax revenue and water scarcity
sections.summary: A question is asked about what carbon tax revenue will fund, alongside a call to update the water scarcity narrative.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: What will the carbon tax revenue be used for?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the old mantra of water scarcity and the danger of the tap being turned off as a result of a breakdown in relations with Malaysia are in need of an upgrade.

sections.label: Lowering household water consumption
sections.summary: Household water consumption is falling, and the speaker suggests extending free initiatives during major HDB upgrading exercises to cut consumption further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Water consumption trends for households are on a downward trend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe there is scope to lower our per capita domestic water consumption even further than the 140 litres per person by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the initiative is provided free of charge, can we not look at extending such initiatives when major Housing and Development Board (HDB) upgrading exercises, such as the Home Improvement Programme (HIP), are carried out in view of the scale of benefits that can be achieved, potentially resulting in lower water consumption?

sections.label: PUB minimum water pressure review
sections.summary: PUB completed a review and concluded it was not useful to set a minimum pressure requirement across all residential units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Last November, it was reported that PUB had finished with the review and concluded that it was not useful to stipulate a minimum pressure requirement across all residential units.

sections.label: Water pressure in HDB flats
sections.summary: The speaker urges PUB to review its decision and set a minimum water pressure for individual HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: These numbers do say a lot that most Singaporeans do play their part to conserve water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge PUB to review its decision and set a minimum pressure for the supply of water to individual HDB flats, for it is not right to expect selected residential units to be the poster boy for water conservation only.

sections.label: Cape Town water restrictions
sections.summary: Cape Town implemented new water restrictions asking residents to curb usage to 50 litres per day, with Day Zero predicted by 16 April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, Cape Town implemented new water restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Residents are asked to curb water usage to 50 litres per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: If water levels continue to fall, it is predicted that the city will run out of water by 16 April, which has been named "Day Zero".

sections.label: Water tariff hike impact
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister what impact last July's water tariff hike had on consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can the Minister tell us what impact the hike in water tariffs last July have on consumption?

sections.label: Annual water rationing exercise proposal
sections.summary: The speaker quotes Mr Leong Sai Mooi on 1960s water rationing and asks if the Minister will reconsider an annual island-wide water rationing exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Borrowing the words of Mr Leong Sai Mooi, who was interviewed when he was 65, as he recounted the water rationing days of the 1960s, I quote him, "Back then, every morning, I worry that the tap would not work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It made me realise how important water was and never to take it for granted." As I have suggested in earlier debates, will the Minister reconsider conducting an annual water rationing exercise island-wide to households and businesses, to build water, physical and mental resilience?

sections.label: Imported water and reservoir supply
sections.summary: Imported water from Malaysia is one of four National Taps, and this reservoir supplies over 60% of water and is threatened by climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Imported water from Malaysia is one of our four National Taps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This reservoir supplies over 60% of our water and is being threatened by climate change.

sections.label: NEWater and desalination by 2060
sections.summary: NEWater and desalination plants will meet up to 85% of water demand by 2060.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: NEWater and desalination plants will meet up to 85% of our water demand by 2060.

sections.label: Unaccounted-for-water losses
sections.summary: Unaccounted-for-water losses are among the lowest in the world at 5%, and the Ministry is hoped to keep exploring ways to reduce losses further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While unaccounted-for-water losses is among the lowest in the world at 5%, I hope the Ministry will continue to explore ways to reduce our losses further.

sections.label: Water per capita target
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore is on track to reduce water per capita from 148 litres to 140 litres by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Are we on track to reach our target of reducing water per capita from 148 litres to 140 litres by 2030?

sections.label: PUB leakage detection sensors
sections.summary: PUB had installed 320 sensors for real-time monitoring to detect leakages from the water supply network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: PUB had installed 320 sensors for real-time monitoring to detect leakages from our water supply network.

sections.label: Drainage works and retention tanks
sections.summary: The Minister mentioned 73 locations with drainage improvement works, 22 more planned this year, and about 500 retention tank submissions with only 158 completed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last month, the Minister also mentioned that there were 73 locations undergoing drainage improvement works, with 22 more planned this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition, he said that there were about 500 submissions for plans to do retention tanks for developments above 0.2 hectares, out of which only 158 have been completed.

sections.label: E-waste recycling update
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on plans to recycle 60,000 tonnes of annual e-waste, noting only 6% of household e-waste is recycled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the plans to recycle the 60,000 tonnes of e-waste that we produce annually?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Only 6% of our household e-waste, which accounts about half of the total, is sent for recycling.

sections.label: Residents and e-waste recycling
sections.summary: Residents said they do not quite know what to do after their karung guni man retired, and 60,000 tonnes of e-waste is generated yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Some residents have told me that much as they would like to recycle, after their neighbourhood karung guni man retired, they sometimes do not quite know what to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that 60,000 tonnes of e-waste is generated in Singapore each year and this number will only rise in the coming years.

sections.label: Microplastics in Singapore beaches
sections.summary: Microplastics have been detected in four beaches and seven mangrove habitats in Singapore's marine sediments and waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, in marine sediments and waters, microplastics have been detected in four beaches and in seven mangrove habitats in Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore plastic waste recycling rate
sections.summary: In 2015, 824,600 tonnes of plastic waste was generated but just 7% were recycled, roughly unchanged since 2001.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, 824,600 tonnes of plastic waste was generated but just 7% were recycled, a proportion roughly unchanged since 2001.

sections.label: Britain plastic carrier bag charge
sections.summary: In Britain, usage of plastic carrier bags fell by 83% after a plastic carrier charge was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Britain, usage of plastic carrier bags fell by 83%, after the introduction of a plastic carrier charge.

sections.label: Taiwan single-use plastics ban
sections.summary: Taiwan announced a blanket ban on single-use plastics, including straws, cups and shopping bags, by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Taiwan has just announced a blanket ban in single-use plastics, including straws, cups and shopping bags, by 2030.

sections.label: Singapore 2016 plastic waste recycling
sections.summary: In Singapore, more than 822,000 tonnes of plastic waste were generated in 2016 but only 7% was recycled.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Miss Cheng Li Hui, you can take your two cuts together.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: It was reported that, in Singapore, more than 822,000 tonnes of plastic waste were generated in 2016 but only 7% of that was recycled.

sections.label: Singapore food delivery app war
sections.summary: Deliveroo, UberEats and Foodpanda ramped up food delivery services, with Deliveroo creating 4,000 rider jobs and planning 3,000 more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, there have been news reports about a food delivery app war in Singapore with tech companies Deliveroo, UberEats and Foodpanda ramping up their food delivery services here.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was reported in The Straits Times in November 2017 that Deliveroo created jobs for 4,000 riders and planned to create 3,000 more.

sections.label: NEA disposable packaging study
sections.summary: The NEA's study of disposable food packaging materials and their environmental impact was supposed to be conducted and concluded in late 2017.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The NEA's study of disposable food packaging materials and their environmental impact was supposed to be conducted and concluded in late 2017.

sections.label: New hawker centres, committee
sections.summary: The Government announced its intention to build 20 new hawker centres by 2027 and appointed a Hawker Centre 3.0 Committee last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Government announced its intention to build 20 new hawker centres by 2027 and appointed a Hawker Centre 3.0 Committee last year to look into improving the management of hawker centres and to sustain the trade.

sections.label: Hawkers' high median age
sections.summary: The hawker trade needed younger and new entrants to sustain it due to the relatively high median age of 59 years old for existing hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Due to the relatively high median age of 59 years old for existing hawkers, the hawker trade needed younger and new entrants into the trade to sustain.

sections.label: Productivity initiatives, Hawkers' Productivity Grant
sections.summary: Many productivity initiatives would require significant cash outlay upfront and may increase operating costs for hawkers, and the Hawkers' Productivity Grant is on the NEA website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, many of the productivity initiatives would also require significant cash outlay upfront and may increase operating costs for the hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I read at the NEA website of the Hawkers' Productivity Grant.

sections.label: NEA summonses increase
sections.summary: Last year, NEA reported an increase in the number of summonses and more than 31,000 summonses were issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Last year, NEA reported an increase in the number of summonses and more than 31,000 summonses were issued.

sections.label: Litter picking, Corrective Work Order
sections.summary: The speaker suggests an annual litter-picking exercise for secondary school students and asks if NEA can consider a mandatory Corrective Work Order for every litterbug caught instead of a fine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If the existing efforts of NEA have not resulted in a cleaner Singapore, then perhaps we should review our efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I suggest that every cohort of secondary school students undergo an annual exercise to pick up litter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can NEA consider imposing a mandatory Corrective Work Order (CWO) for every litterbug caught instead of imposing a fine?

sections.label: Foreign worker littering work pass
sections.summary: Asks whether NEA can treat littering by foreign workers as an adverse record when renewing their work pass, combining education with punitive action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For every foreign worker caught for littering, can NEA consider it as an adverse record when deciding whether to renew their work pass?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We need to combine our educational efforts with adequate punitive actions.

sections.label: Warm 2017 and rainfall
sections.summary: States 2017 was the warmest non El-Nino year at home, and on 8 January half the month's average rain fell in four hours in Singapore while little fell over Linggiu Reservoir.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: At home, 2017 was the warmest non El-Nino year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On 8 January, half the month’s average rainfall fell over four hours in Singapore but little rain fell over Linggiu Reservoir.

sections.label: Public Sector Sustainability Plan targets
sections.summary: The Public Sector Sustainability Plan set targets to save electricity and water and green buildings, and targets will expand to waste reduction and solar energy adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Last year, we launched the Public Sector Sustainability Plan, setting out targets to save electricity and water and green our buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will do more by expanding our targets to include waste reduction and solar energy adoption.

sections.label: Adaptation to climate change
sections.summary: Adaptation to cope with climate change impact involves continuing to invest billions in infrastructure such as raising coastal roads, enhancing stormwater systems and diversifying water supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: First, adaptation, to cope with the impact of climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have and will continue to invest billions of dollars in infrastructure, such as raising our coastal roads, enhancing stormwater systems and diversifying our water supply.

sections.label: Stock level improved to 63%
sections.summary: The stock level gradually improved to 63% over more than a year, mainly due to good rainfall and completion of the Johor River Barrage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: While the stock level has gradually improved to 63%, it took more than a year, mainly due to good rainfall and the completion of the Johor River Barrage.

sections.label: Weather-resilient water sources
sections.summary: Water supply was augmented with weather-resilient sources NEWater and desalinated water; the third Tuas desalination plant comes online this year, with two more by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Over the years, we augmented our water supply with weather-resilient sources – NEWater and desalinated water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This year, our third desalination plant in Tuas will come online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: By 2020, we will have two more, taking the total to five.

sections.label: Carbon emissions savings from integration
sections.summary: Integration will save more than 200,000 tonnes of carbon emissions a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Through integration, we will save more than 200,000 tonnes of carbon emissions a year.

sections.label: Singapore household water consumption drop
sections.summary: Singapore's household water consumption fell from 148 litres in 2016 to 143 litres per person per day in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Now, they are struggling to cut back to 50 litres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I am encouraged by the drop in Singapore’s household consumption from 148 litres in 2016 to 143 litres per person per day in 2017.

sections.label: Households benefit from water savings
sections.summary: One thousand one hundred households benefited and saw a 10% reduction in water bills on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: One thousand one hundred households have already benefited and saw a 10% reduction in water bills on average.

sections.label: Smart shower devices demonstration project
sections.summary: Up to 10,000 new homes will get smart shower devices; an NUS pilot of 500 households saved five litres per person daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Up to 10,000 new homes will be equipped with smart shower devices under a demonstration project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: A National University of Singapore (NUS) pilot involving 500 households showed water savings of five litres per person per day on average.

sections.label: Diversion canal and tank works
sections.summary: Works at Stamford Diversion Canal, Stamford Detention Tank and Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal will be completed in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The works at Stamford Diversion Canal, Stamford Detention Tank and Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal will be completed in 2018.

sections.label: Dengue cases drop in 2017
sections.summary: Stakeholder effort against the 2016 Zika outbreak and vector control contributed to dengue cases in 2017 being almost five times lower than 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The concerted effort by all stakeholders in response to the 2016 Zika outbreak and our vector control actions contributed to the drop in the number of dengue cases in 2017, almost five times lower than in 2016.

sections.label: Train access and car population
sections.summary: By 2030, eight in 10 households will live within 10 minutes of a train station, and car population growth was frozen last month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: By 2030, eight in 10 households will live within 10 minutes of a train station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have frozen the growth of our car population starting last month.

sections.label: KPMG study on carbon targets
sections.summary: A KPMG study found that only 17% of local firms have carbon reduction targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: A KPMG study found that only 17% of local firms have carbon reduction targets.

sections.label: Louis Ng asks carbon tax rate
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng asked how the starting tax rate of $5 per tonne was decided, which is intended to rise to $10 to $15 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked how we decided on the starting tax rate of $5 per tonne, which we intend to raise to $10 to $15 by 2030.

sections.label: Companies affected by GHG measures
sections.summary: Around 40 companies, accounting for about 80% of Singapore's GHG emissions, will be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Around 40 companies, which account for about 80% of Singapore’s GHG emissions, will be affected.

sections.label: EPR recycling and disposal responsibility
sections.summary: The EPR approach extends manufacturers' and importers' responsibility to recycling and disposal of products at end-of-life, incentivising longer-lasting, recyclable designs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The EPR approach extends their responsibility to include the proper recycling and disposal of their products at the end-of-life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Manufacturers and importers will take charge of the waste they had produced, rather than the society bearing the costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: By doing so, businesses are also incentivised to design products that last longer and can be more easily recycled.

sections.label: Special ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Climate Action
sections.summary: Singapore will convene a Special ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Climate Action on 10 July 2018 and a back-to-back expanded meeting with ASEAN and other ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Singapore will convene a Special ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Climate Action on 10 July 2018, and a back-to-back expanded meeting with ASEAN and Ministers from China, Japan, Korea and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) of the Conference of the Parties (COP) President and President-designate Fiji and Poland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: These will take place in conjunction with the Singapore International Water Week (SIWW) – CleanEnviro Summit Singapore (CESG) – World Cities Summit joint event.

sections.label: Year of Climate Action
sections.summary: 2018 is designated the Year of Climate Action to raise national consciousness on climate change across generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This is akin to our Water Story, which was not just the effort of the Government, but that of generations of Singaporeans who partnered us for the greater good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This is why we have designated 2018 as the Year of Climate Action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It is the start of our journey to raise the level of national consciousness to fight climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will pass this consciousness from generation to generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This will ensure our children do not end up facing a climate change crisis – higher sea levels, frequent swings between intense weather or pestilence.

sections.label: Climate action for children
sections.summary: Taking climate action now passes to children a liveable city with low carbon businesses and sought-after environmental solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Taking climate action now is how we shall pass to our children a Singapore that is a liveable city ever more, a city where thriving businesses have low carbon footprints, and a city with environmental solutions that are well sought after.

sections.label: Climate Action video views
sections.summary: Since January, MEWR's Facebook video received over 160,000 views and more than 21,000 individuals made Climate Action pledges online.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Since the Year of Climate Action was launched in January, the video on MEWR's Facebook page has received over 160,000 views, and I am glad that more than 21,000 individuals have made Climate Action pledges online.

sections.label: Climate Action SG Alliance
sections.summary: Ms Jessica Cheam brought together NGOs and business leaders to form the Climate Action SG Alliance to advocate climate action.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Arising from this dialogue, Ms Jessica Cheam, Managing Editor of Eco-Business, brought together NGOs and business leaders to form the Climate Action SG Alliance to advocate climate action and raise public awareness on climate issues.

sections.label: Funding and company pledges
sections.summary: Eligible organisations can get up to $5,000 on reimbursement, and over 110 firms made Climate Action SG pledges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Upon application, each eligible organisation can be provided with up to $5,000 on a reimbursement basis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Many companies have reached out to us in support of the Year of Climate Action, with over 110 firms, including the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS), SembCorp, City Developments Ltd (CDL) and Ricoh, making Climate Action SG pledges.

sections.label: Singapore e-waste generated
sections.summary: Singapore generates about 60,000 tonnes of e-waste annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Singapore generates about 60,000 tonnes of e-waste annually.

sections.label: Mandatory e-waste management system
sections.summary: MEWR will implement a mandatory e-waste management system by 2021 covering five product categories, including ICT equipment, solar panels, batteries, lamps and large appliances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MEWR will implement a mandatory e-waste management system by 2021 to ensure that electrical and electronic products are disposed of in an environmentally friendly way and allow for safe recovery of useful materials.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For a start, this system will cover five main categories of products, namely, information and communications technology (ICT) equipment like mobile phones and computers, solar panels, batteries, lamps and certain large household appliances like refrigerators, air-conditioners, washing machines and dryers.

sections.label: NEA collection targets for manufacturers
sections.summary: NEA will set collection targets for manufacturers and importers to take back a proportion of the products they put on the market.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NEA will set collection targets for manufacturers and importers to take back a proportion of the products they put on the market.

sections.label: Supporting smaller industry players
sections.summary: Smaller industry players, including karung guni men, will be integrated and supported to benefit from the national system, and food waste recycling rose from 12% in 2012 to 16% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will integrate and support smaller industry players so they can benefit from our national system, including the karung guni men who provide collection services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I am glad that our food waste recycling rate has increased from 12% in 2012 to 16% in 2017, which is about 133,000 tonnes.

sections.label: Packaging waste reporting framework
sections.summary: A mandatory reporting framework for packaging waste management will be put in place by 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Building on this, we will put in place a mandatory reporting framework for packaging waste management by 2021.

sections.label: Lifecycle assessment on disposable bags
sections.summary: An NEA-commissioned LCA study found all disposable bag types impose different environmental impacts, so charging or banning plastic bags and substituting other disposable bags is unlikely to improve outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: A recently concluded lifecycle assessment (LCA) study on carrier bags and food packaging, commissioned by NEA, found that every type of disposable bag, not just plastic bags, but also bio-degradable bags and paper bags, for example, impose different environmental impacts, whether it be carbon emissions, heavy water usage or significant land clearance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This is particularly so as we incinerate our waste and we do not directly landfill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Hence, imposing a charge or ban on disposable plastic bags and substituting them with other types of disposable bags is unlikely to improve environmental outcomes.

sections.label: Businesses report packaging by 2021
sections.summary: By 2021, businesses will be mandated to report the type and amount of packaging they put on the market and their reduction plans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: By 2021, we will mandate that businesses report on the type and amount of packaging they put on the market and their plans for reduction.

sections.label: Littering fines and enforcement
sections.summary: The maximum littering fine was doubled in 2014 and enforcement tickets rose to over 32,000 last year from around 26,000 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2014, we doubled the maximum fine for littering offences under the Environmental Public Health Act (EPHA) to enhance deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have stepped up enforcement against littering over the years, issuing more than 32,000 tickets last year compared to around 26,000 in 2015.

sections.label: Food delivery regulations
sections.summary: There are no immediate plans to introduce additional regulations over food delivery services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Given these, we have no immediate plans to introduce additional regulations over food delivery services.

sections.label: Hawker centre upgrading and building
sections.summary: The $420 million Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme upgraded over 100 centres by 2013, and 20 new centres are planned by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2001, the Government also started a $420 million Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme (HUP) and upgraded more than 100 hawker centres by the end of the programme in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We announced in 2015 that we will build 20 new hawker centres by 2027, and since then, seven new hawker centres have opened, including three last year in Woodlands, Yishun and Jurong West and one in Pasir Ris this year.

sections.label: Stall meal prices
sections.summary: In almost all the new centres, more than 90% of stalls offer meal options at $3 or below.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In almost all the new centres, more than 90% of the stalls offer such meal options at $3 or below.

sections.label: Hawker productivity funding
sections.summary: About $90 million is set aside for hawker productivity, with hawkers reimbursed 80% of qualifying equipment costs up to $5,000 within three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Government has set aside about $90 million to enhance productivity in hawker centres through stall- and centre-level initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Hawkers can be reimbursed 80% of the qualifying cost of equipment, up to a sum of $5,000, within three years.

sections.label: Tray return encouragement
sections.summary: Tray return encouragement began in 2012 mainly to ease cleaners' work, speed table turnover and benefit patrons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: There has been much public discussion about the rationale and merit of encouraging tray return.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We started encouraging tray return in 2012, primarily to ease the work of cleaners so that they can concentrate on cleaning tables, allowing for faster turnover of the tables which will benefit patrons.

sections.label: Tray return nudges pilot
sections.summary: A project using behavioural nudges and visual cues to improve tray return rates was piloted at Zion Riverside and Adam Food Centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: At the same time, we have piloted a project at Zion Riverside Food Centre and Adam Food Centre using behavioural "nudges" and visual cues to improve tray return rates.

sections.label: Tray return rate increase
sections.summary: At Zion Riverside Food Centre the tray return rate rose by about 20%, and NEA will roll out these initiatives to more hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: At Zion Riverside Food Centre, the tray return rate increased by about 20%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NEA will roll out these initiatives to more hawker centres.

sections.label: Events across hawker centres
sections.summary: The response was enthusiastic, and some 19 events took place across 12 hawker centres in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The response has been enthusiastic, and some 19 events had taken place across 12 hawker centres in 2017.

sections.label: Light bulbs and Khatib littering
sections.summary: Details for replacing light bulbs for 1- and 2-roomers are being worked out, and NEA staff are working with grassroots on Khatib basketball court littering, where CCTV cameras are installed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the light bulbs, we are working out the details, taking feedback from retailers, as well as with the community, NGOs and companies who may want to do CSR on how we can more effectively implement the replacement of the light bulbs for the 1- and 2-roomers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regarding littering issues in the basketball courts at Khatib, I am given to understand that the North West Regional Office staff from NEA are working closely with the Member's grassroots to address the littering problem at the courts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I think the issue is that there are multiple parties using the courts and it is very difficult to identify who the litterbugs are.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But I know that closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras have already been installed.

sections.label: Water target 140 litres
sections.summary: There is a target of 140 litres per capita per day by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The first question is whether we will revise the target or do we have a target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have a target of 140 litres per capita per day, as inferred by Mr Pritam Singh, by 2030.

sections.label: No particular number decided
sections.summary: Because of complications such as reticulation, appliances, room sizes and occupancy, the professionals, engineers, industry, consultants and PUB decided not to put up a particular number.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: There are many other issues ‒ how reticulation will be laid out, the kind of appliances that would be used, the sizes of the rooms, the number of people in the room ‒ fairly complicated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Therefore, the decision of this body of professionals, engineers, the industry, consultants, as well as PUB, finally decided that we should not put up a particular number.

sections.label: Public cleanliness perception survey results
sections.summary: The public cleanliness perception survey showed 82% of respondents were satisfied with Singapore's overall cleanliness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In the public cleanliness perception survey, it actually showed that 82% of the respondents said that they were satisfied with the overall cleanliness of Singapore ‒ hard as it may be for you.

sections.label: Littering offenders and repeat rates
sections.summary: Of about 30,000 littering offenders caught in 2017, about 5% were repeat offenders, and about 10% of those who had done CWOs were repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: If you look at enforcement, for the 30,000-odd littering offenders caught in 2017, for instance, about 5% are repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Of those who have done CWOs before, repeat offenders are about 10%.

sections.label: Coastal protection study and plastic bags
sections.summary: The coastal protection study will be ready by 2018, and a question asks if MEWR will further study single-use plastic bag usage and implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: When the coastal protection study is ready by 2018, we will see the details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can I ask if MEWR will be studying the issue of the usage of single-used plastic bags further, especially with regard to implementing the usage plan?

sections.label: Tackling disposables at source
sections.summary: Measures include mandatory reporting of packaging waste and business waste reduction plans by 2021, working with VWOs to raise awareness, and disallowing disposable crockeries for dining-in at new hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: What we want to do is to tackle it at source.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we will have mandatory reporting of packaging waste, as well as the waste reduction plans by businesses by 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In addition, we will work with the voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and other organisations to raise awareness and encourage people to reduce their use of such disposables.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In our new hawker centres, for instance, we have already disallowed use of disposable crockeries and so on for dining-in.

sections.label: Court issues corrective work orders
sections.summary: The CWO is issued by the Court, and for repeat offenders who go to Court, CWOs are recommended.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The CWO is actually issued by the Court.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, if they are repeat offenders, they go to Court and we do recommend CWOs.
